Article Title: 'Next target is to finish Dimagi Naxals': Kiren Rijiju slams Rahul Gandhi for attacking PM Modi
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Union minister Kiren Rijiju on Tuesday slammed Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi for attacking Prime Minister Narendra Modi over his remarks on 'Dimagi Naxal'.In a social media post on X, Rijiju reminded Rahul that former Prime Minister Manmohan Singh had described Left-wing extremism as the biggest internal security threat to the country."Rahul ji, thank Modi ji for eliminating the Armed Maoists. Former PM Dr Manmohan Singh ji had famously described Left-Wing Extremism and Naxalism as 'The single biggest internal security threat' to India," Rijiju said."Next target is to finish Dimagi Naxals," he added.This comes a day after Rahul hit back at PM Modi over his 'Dimagi Naxal' remarks, claiming that the CRPF jawans' facial expressions suggested they did not believe the Prime Minister's claims.In a post on X addressed to CRPF personnel who attended PM Modi's Diwali event in Bastar, Rahul said, "Your faces said it all: you didn't buy the PM's lies. He called us Naxals.""My challenge stands. Let him debate me on who is anti-national and who is controlled by foreign forces. Any time, any place," he said, adding, "My guarantee: after the debate, the PM won't have the guts to stand in front of a single jawan again."The war of words began after PM Modi, while celebrating Diwali with security personnel in Bastar, Chhattisgarh, said that although armed Naxalites had been wiped out from forests, "Dimagi Naxals" had infiltrated several organisations and political parties and were inciting people against the Constitution and democracy.The Prime Minister also accused previous governments of restricting the freedom of security personnel engaged in anti-Naxal operations, saying his government had given them the authority to take necessary decisions."We must remember one thing. Naxalites have been eliminated, but the threat is not yet over. While armed Naxalites have been wiped out from the forests, 'Dimagi Naxals' have taken control of several organisations. Even today, they are inciting people against the country's Constitution and democracy. These 'Dimagi Naxals' have also infiltrated several political parties and different organisations. We must identify them, defeat them and ensure the security of the nation," PM Modi said.The remarks came months after the Centre announced on March 31 that the country had been freed from the menace of Naxalism, following the elimination of several Maoist leaders and cadres and the surrender of hundreds of others.
Article Summary: Rijiju reminded Rahul that former PM Manmohan Singh had described Left-wing extremism as the biggest internal security threat to the country. Rahul hit back at PM Modi over his 'Dimagi Naxal' remarks, claiming that the CRPF jawans' facial expressions suggested they did not believe the Prime Minister's claims.

Article Title: Sonia Gandhi memoir: BJP's Phoolka questions Army timeline, Indira's tears on 1984 riots
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: BJP leader and senior advocate HS Phoolka has challenged Congress leader Sonia Gandhi's account of the 1984 anti-Sikh violence and Operation Blue Star in her memoir, Belonging: A Journey of Love, alleging that some of the details contradict official records and historical documents.He has questioned her account of when the Army was called in following Indira Gandhi's assassination and also disputed her description of the former prime minister's emotional reaction to Operation Blue Star.Speaking to news agency ANI, Phoolka said he had received several calls from media organisations seeking his response to Sonia Gandhi's account that the Army was called in on October 31, 1984, the day then prime minister Indira Gandhi was assassinated."I got several phone calls from media. They said Sonia Gandhi has written that during the 1984 Sikh massacre, the Army was called on 31st October itself. I have purchased the book to read whether this is indeed written in the book. If this is written in the book, it is against the records. It is absolutely false," Phoolka told ANI.Referring to the Misra Commission's findings, Phoolka maintained that the Army was formally called in only on the evening of November 1 and reached the affected areas in significant numbers on November 2.Phoolka also cited the commission's observations on the availability of Army personnel in Delhi during the violence."Misra Commission stated that 5,000 Army personnel were available within Delhi and they were not deployed. Misra Commission stated that had they been deployed, lives of 2,000 Sikhs could have been saved," he said.The Misra Commission found that an additional Army brigade of around 1,600 personnel had reached Delhi from Meerut before midnight on October 31, 1984.However, the Delhi administration delayed formally requisitioning Army assistance. The Army became operational in parts of central and south Delhi by the evening of November 1, while five additional brigades arrived on November 2. The commission observed that deploying around 5,000 available Army personnel on the morning of November 1 could have prevented at least 2,000 deaths."Phoolka also questioned Sonia Gandhi's account of Indira Gandhi's alleged remorse following Operation Blue Star, the military operation carried out at the Golden Temple complex in Amritsar in June 1984.In her memoir, Sonia Gandhi reportedly recounts seeing Indira Gandhi watching a slow-motion recording of the operation's aftermath, with tears in her eyes. She describes the former prime minister's emotional reaction as an expression of pain and regret over the loss of lives during the operation.Disputing this account, Phoolka said it did not appear to be consistent with the historical record. He referred to a fact-finding report prepared by a team led by former Supreme Court judge Justice VM Tarkunde in September 1984, which he said included postmortem reports documenting the aftermath of the military operation."This doesn't seem to be true. In September, Justice Tarkunde's team wrote a fact-finding report on Operation Blue Star. Actual postmortem report was included in the report. The entire team was arrested and the report was banned," he told ANI.Questioning the account of Indira Gandhi's remorse, Phoolka further said, "If you look at the actual facts, you won't find any regrets or tears. It might be crocodile tears."
Article Summary: HS Phoolka has challenged Congress leader Sonia Gandhi's account of 1984 anti- Sikh violence and Operation Blue Star in her memoir. He has questioned her account of when the Army was called in following Indira Gandhi's assassination and also disputed her description of the former prime minister's emotional reaction to the operation. He said the Misra Commission's findings on the availability of Army personnel in Delhi during the violence did not seem to be true.

Article Title: Three workers killed during water tank maintenance at Tata iPhone parts factory in Tamil Nadu
Article Text:
Three workers died in an incident at Tata Electronics' facility in Hosur, Tamil Nadu.

NEW DELHI: Three contract workers died on Monday evening after drowning while carrying out maintenance and cleaning work inside a nano-filtration feed tank at Tata Marigold Company in Vanniyapuram, Krishnagiri district, Tamil Nadu The deceased were identified as Kaveri, 28, J Akmal, 28, and Sarath Kumar, 25, all residents of Rayakottai. They were cleaning the tank when the incident occurred.“They were immediately rescued and rushed to a nearby hospital. However, doctors declared them brought dead,” Krishnagiri district collector C Dinesh Kumar said.State minister Virudhai Magal Keerthana expressed grief over the deaths and said she had spoken to the district administration to ensure support for the affected families.“Deeply saddened by the tragic loss of three precious lives in the incident at Tata Electronics' facility in Hosur...I have spoken to the district administration and directed them to extend all necessary support to the affected families and ensure that the situation is addressed with utmost urgency,” she said.“The safety and dignity of every worker must remain paramount. This tragic incident will be thoroughly investigated, and appropriate action will be taken based on the findings.We must ensure that every necessary measure is put in place to prevent such tragedies from recurring,” the minister added.Authorities have launched an inquiry to establish the circumstances leading to the incident and determine whether there were any lapses in industrial safety protocols at the facility. Rayakottai police have registered a case and initiated an investigation. The district administration and police are also monitoring the situation around the industrial unit to maintain law and order.Following an update on the probe from Apple, the company's team visited the Tata factory to investigate the incident, a person familiar with the matter told Reuters.Tata Electronics, an Apple supplier, has also reportedly been instructed to conduct a comprehensive review of the performance and safety compliance of the agencies responsible for maintaining the Effluent Treatment Plant (ETP).
Article Summary: Three contract workers died on Monday evening after drowning while carrying out maintenance and cleaning work inside a nano-filtration feed tank at Tata Marigold Company in Vanniyapuram, Krishnagiri district, Tamil Nadu. Authorities have launched an inquiry to establish the circumstances leading to the incident. Apple has also reportedly been instructed to conduct a comprehensive review of the performance and safety compliance of the agencies responsible for maintaining the Effluent Treatment Plant.

Article Title: Hasina seeks passport, Dhaka calls it political stunt & seeks extradition
Article Text:
Kobir said there is no scope now for staging drama in the name of returning to the country using the passport issue (Photo: Reuters).

DHAKA/NEW DELHI: India-Bangladesh ties may experience fresh turbulence with ousted PM Sheikh Hasina 's legal counsel formally requesting a new passport and national identity card from the Bangladesh High Commission in New Delhi to facilitate her return to the country. While the high commission said it wasn't sure if the request was genuine as it was not backed by supporting documents, Dhaka responded by declaring it doesn't issue passports to "convicted terrorists" and reiterating its demand for Hasina's extradition.India, however, sees the passport request as a matter purely between the government in Dhaka and a Bangladeshi national, one that should not be conflated with her extradition issue. The Indian government maintains that Hasina's extradition is subject to established legal and judicial processes under the bilateral extradition treaty.Hasina had earlier announced that she planned to 'return' to Bangladesh in December. However, India is likely to distance itself from Hasina's passport bid - described by Bangladesh authorities as a political stunt - as it believes this will be Dhaka's call entirely."She has fled after killing people. One who has fled, how would she come? How would a terrorist come? There’s an extradition treaty. Handover would be sought through the treaty," said Bangladesh's state minister for foreign affairs Humaiun Kobir.Kobir said there is no scope now for staging drama in the name of returning to the country using the passport issue.“If she truly wishes to return, there is a specific legal process for doing so. An extradition treaty exists between Bangladesh and India; she should ask the Indian government to hand her over to Bangladesh under the terms of that treaty. She should return, surrender to the court, and serve her sentence,” he said.Political insiders in Dhaka say the government and opposition party Jamaat do not actually want Hasina’s return at this moment and that is why the government is unwilling to accept her voluntary return and tagging extradition treaty issue which is time-consuming and complicated.In 2025, a Bangladeshi special tribunal sentenced her to death for crimes against humanity, ruling that she was responsible for ordering the crackdown, which left hundreds of people dead and thousands of others injured.Hasina requested a new passport on Monday to facilitate her return from exile two years after she was ousted in a mass uprising.In a letter, emailed to the Bangladesh High Commission in New Delhi, Hasina’s counsel urged the top diplomat to take necessary action to provide her with a passport and national identity card.The letter, sent by London-based law firm Matrix Chambers, asked the mission for the application to be processed “expeditiously” on the basis of Hasina’s Bangladeshi nationality and in accordance with “obligations arising under international human rights instruments.”The letter, sent via email and addressed to Acting High Commissioner Preeti Rahman, was shared with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.Hasina’s application is ridiculous, State Minister Kobir said, criticising the British law firm over its involvement in the matter.“Know your client. Don’t run after her looted money from the people of Bangladesh. Exercise some ethical and moral boundaries. And if you don’t have those boundaries, you will be shamed all over the world,” he said.“If death is my destiny, I would rather die on the soil of my own country, among my own people,” Hasina told AP in response to questions by email. “So, I will return to Bangladesh. That decision has not changed.”
Article Summary: Ousted PM Sheikh Hasina's legal counsel formally requested a new passport and national identity card from the Bangladesh High Commission in New Delhi. Dhaka responded by declaring it doesn't issue passports to "convicted terrorists" India, however, sees the passport request as a matter purely between the government in Dhaka and a Bangladeshi national.

Article Title: Ahead of peace talks, Zelenskyy seeks PM Modi's help on ceasefire
Article Text:
PM Narendra Modi and Ukraine President Volodymyr Zelenskyy spoke Monday

NEW DELHI: Ahead of the Abu Dhabi peace talks, PM Narendra Modi and Ukraine President Volodymyr Zelenskyy spoke Monday with the latter briefing the PM about latest developments related to the Russia-Ukraine conflict and Modi conveying India’s "firm commitment" to contributing in every possible way towards a peaceful resolution of the Russia-Ukraine war.The conversation took place a day before the trilateral peace dialogue involving Russia, Ukraine and the US in Abu Dhabi, and amid renewed Russian strikes on Ukraine's energy infrastructure. Ahead of the talks, where India's recent peace proposals are likely to be discussed too, India remained engaged with both sides on diplomatic initiatives as foreign minister S Jaishankar too spoke to his Russian counterpart Sergey Lavrov.Zelenskyy recalled Modi's latest peace message to President Vladimir Putin that it was time now to end the "endless war" and urged India to take more steps towards a ceasefire that can ensure food and energy security. Modi said in a post on X that he and Zelenskyy had a productive conversation – their first since they met on the margins of the G7 summit in France in June.Modi's message to Zelenskyy expressing India's readiness to facilitate peace is not new, but its timing is significant as this was the first time they spoke after Jaishankar revealed in early October India was actively mediating for establishment of safe corridors in the Black Sea for grain and energy exports."We reviewed our wide-ranging bilateral cooperation and agreed to further strengthen India-Ukraine ties. I thanked President Zelenskyy for sharing his perspectives on the ongoing conflict, its humanitarian aspects and various efforts to restore peace," said Modi in his own readout of the talks.Ukraine believes Russia has not responded positively to India's Black Sea shipping proposal and the call to end targeting of its energy sector. "The Prime Minister has said more than once, including directly to the Russian ‌leader, ⁠that now is the time to end the war, not to continue it," said Zelenskyy on X after his talks with Modi, urging India to identify steps it can take and also talks it can pursue with other leaders to bring the conflict to an end.“Food security could be one such area. We discussed Russia's blocking of grain exports via the Black Sea. India is ready to mediate in establishing food corridors, and we are counting on these efforts to continue,” said the Ukrainian president.Zelenskyy also said Ukraine had always taken a constructive approach, and Russia must show the same readiness to de-escalate.“Russia must understand that the global economy and hundreds of millions of people around the world are suffering because of blocked sea routes. We agreed that our teams will stay in touch on these and other bilateral issues,” he said.An Indian readout said Modi reaffirmed India’s human-centric approach and reiterated India’s consistent position that the conflict must be resolved through dialogue and diplomacy.The 4th round of Russia-Ukraine peace talks mediated by the US are scheduled to begin in Abu Dhabi on Tuesday. While the core negotiations are structured as trilateral sessions involving Russia, Ukraine, and the US, Ukrainian delegation will hold separate coordination meetings with their European and Nato allies including France, Germany and the UK on the sidelines.
Article Summary: PM Narendra Modi and Ukraine President Volodymyr Zelenskyy spoke Monday ahead of the Abu Dhabi peace talks. The conversation took place a day before the trilateral peace dialogue involving Russia, Ukraine and the US in Abu Dhabi. India's recent peace proposals are likely to be discussed too.

NEW DELHI: Former Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina has formally sought a new passport and national identity card (NID), taking a step towards her planned return from India in December.The information comes from a Monday letter sent by Hasina’s lawyers to the acting high commissioner at Bangladesh's embassy in Delhi, Preeti Rahman, Reuters reported.Hasina's lawyers at London-based Matrix Chambers requested the issuance of fresh documents. They cited the reported cancellation of her existing passport and NID by Bangladesh's interim government and other authorities."In view of the reported revocation of her existing Bangladeshi passport and National Identity Card (NID) by the Interim Government and other authorities, I respectfully request that you take the necessary steps to issue a new Bangladeshi passport and National Identity Card for our client," the lawyers wrote.The letter urged the authorities to process the applications "expeditiously", citing Hasina's Bangladeshi nationality and the country's "obligations arising under international human rights instruments".However, Bangladesh denied Hasina’s request, stating that the country does not provide "passport to a terrorist"."She is a fugitive criminal. We have an active extradition treaty with India. We want her handed over," Bangladesh state minister for foreign affairs, Humaiun Kobir, told reporters."Should we treat her like an ordinary commercial traveller and tell her ​to come and visit her ​in-laws’ residence?" Kobir jibed.According to Reuters, the request is the clearest indication yet that Hasina is taking steps to act on her stated intention to return in December, more than two years after a deadly uprising forced her from power. Her return could reignite political and legal tensions as Bangladesh attempts to restore stability and her Awami League party remains banned.Hasina intends to return and surrender before a court. Her aides said on Monday that the date would be announced after the completion of various formalities.Last week, the exiled leader the Associated Press she would prefer dying in her own land, among her own people.“If death is my destiny, I would rather die on the soil of my own country, among my own people,” Hasina said.In November 2025, Bangladesh's war-crimes tribunal sentenced Hasina to death in absentia for ordering a crackdown on the student-led uprising. She has denied the charges, rejected the verdict and questioned the legitimacy of the trial.The crackdown killed hundreds of protesters and left thousands injured. According to United Nations data cited by the Associated Press, nearly 1,400 people were killed during the unrest.Bangladesh has repeatedly sought Hasina's extradition from India. New Delhi has said the request is being examined through legal channels.Hasina's Awami League was Bangladesh's largest political party before it was banned following her removal from office. Several of its leaders and members have since been jailed, while others have gone into self-imposed exile in India and elsewhere.Having served as Prime Minister for 20 years across multiple terms, Hasina retains support among sections of the population. Her return could deepen political divisions as the country continues to deal with the aftermath of the upheaval.It could also have implications for Bangladesh's strained relationship with India, which deteriorated sharply after New Delhi gave the former prime minister refuge.
Article Summary: Sheikh Hasina has formally sought a new passport and national identity card (NID) The request is reportedly the clearest indication yet that Hasina is taking steps to act on her stated intention to return in December. Bangladesh denied Hasina’s request, stating that the country does not provide "passport to a terrorist"

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Monday held a telephone conversation with Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskyy, during which the two leaders discussed the ongoing Russia-Ukraine conflict, recent diplomatic developments and ways to strengthen bilateral cooperation.In a post on X, PM Modi described the conversation as productive and said the two leaders reviewed their wide-ranging bilateral cooperation and agreed to further strengthen India-Ukraine ties. Article Title: 'There is an old saying': BJP MLA Papiya Adhikari explains her 'firecrackers cure illness' remark, apologises

NEW DELHI: West Bengal BJP MLA Papiya Adhikari on Monday defended herself after facing criticism for claiming that bursting firecrackers helps kill germs and viruses.The actor-turned-politician said her statements were being deliberately twisted to garner TRP."Whenever I say something, people who oppose me use it to increase their TRP and views. Even if I cough or sneeze, the 'seku-maku' (a Bengali slang meaning secular and Marxists) pick it up," Adhikari told a Bengali TV channel."What I meant was that bursting firecrackers during Diwali-Kali Puja night kills germs, as told by our grandmothers and elders for generations. Lighting lamps drives away evil forces," she added.Later in the day, the BJP MLA apologised for her remarks and said: "There is an old saying from our ancestors regarding these traditions. In essence, this is a festival of lights - a festival of lighting lamps - meant to eradicate social evils. In the past, through rituals, many such evils were addressed. Now, however, we live in the era of firecrackers, and given how much science has advanced, perhaps that perspective is no longer appropriate."If anyone has been hurt, I apologise. I am willing to retract my statement; consider it withdrawn. But the core idea remains: such social evils were - and still can be - eradicated."Adhikari was trolled for claiming at a Kali Puja pandal inauguration in her Tollygunge constituency on Saturday that bursting firecrackers could cure several diseases.While addressing a gathering, a firecracker exploded loudly in front of her.Continuing her speech, she said, "You will see that bursting firecrackers will cure several diseases. Our chief minister has said that we will burst firecrackers. How can Kali Puja be complete without green firecrackers? We will definitely burst green firecrackers.""However, we will follow the guidelines issued by the police," she added.Chief minister Suvendu Adhikari on Monday said the administration had taken necessary measures to enforce the Supreme Court's guidelines on noise pollution, though he acknowledged that some firecrackers were burst beyond the permitted hours.
Article Summary: West Bengal BJP MLA Papiya Adhikari defended herself after facing criticism for claiming that bursting firecrackers helps kill germs and viruses. The actor- turned-politician said her statements were being deliberately twisted to garner TRP. She apologised for her remarks and said: "There is an old saying from our ancestors regarding these traditions"

Article Title: Reds gone, but 'dimagi Naxals' still instigating people: PM Modi
Article Text:

RAIPUR: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Sunday warned that the end of armed Maoist insurgency did not mean the threat had disappeared, alleging that what he called 'Dimagi Naxals' had infiltrated political parties and organisations and were inciting people against the Constitution and democracyContinuing his long-standing tradition of celebrating Diwali with security forces, this time at Karanpur camp in Chhattisgarh's Bastar - once the epicentre of Maoist insurgency and declared free of Naxalism on March 31 this year - he called for identifying and defeating such elements to safeguard the country.Calling it a historic Diwali after nearly five decades of conflict, Modi said this was the first festival of lights when every district in the country was free from Maoist insurgency. "This is the first Diwali after the country has won its decades-long battle against Naxalism and Maoist terror. This is the first Diwali when every district is free from Naxalism," he said, attributing the achievement to the courage, sacrifices and dedication of security forces.Modi asserted that for the first time in 47 years, the CRPF had completed a year without losing a single jawan in operational duty.He described the milestone as a victory of sound policies, political resolve and the bravery and restraint of security personnel. "More than 1,000 jawans sacrificed their lives in Chhattisgarh", he said, recalling the scale of Maoist violence, adding there was a time when more than 230 districts across 20 states were affected.From Bihar and Odisha to Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh and Chhattisgarh, vast regions had lived under the shadow of violence, he said. "After sunset, life would come to a standstill. People could not step out of their homes. Naxals had even snatched away people's right to vote," he said.Modi recalled the April 2010 Dantewada massacre in which 76 CRPF personnel were killed and another attack that year in which he said 44 civilians lost their lives. He accused previous govts of treating the insurgency as an incurable problem and abandoning tribal communities to their fate. "Some had accepted that bullets would continue to fly, jawans would die and innocent people would suffer. No country can confront its enemies with an attitude that things will simply continue this way," he said.He credited the change in India's counter-insurgency strategy to the political will demonstrated after his government assumed office in 2014. "We gave our security forces the freedom to take every necessary decision," he said, adding the govt had taken several national security decisions, including measures not widely known to the public, to disrupt funding networks supporting Maoists and separatist organisations.He also alleged that elements within the earlier political and administrative system had provided support to Left-Wing Extremism, which his govt worked to eliminate.Linking the decline in insurgency to development, Modi said Maoists had prevented schools, hospitals, medical facilities, mobile towers and industries from coming up in areas under their influence. Modi said the govt had, therefore, pursued security operations alongside a special development campaign.According to him, more than 15,000km of roads had been constructed in areas affected by Naxalism, along with over 9,500 mobile towers. Nearly 175 Eklavya residential schools had been opened for tribal students, while 50 industrial training institutes and approximately 50 skill development centres were established to improve employment opportunities. He also cited the establishment of thousands of post offices, bank branches and ATMs in previously underserved regions.
Article Summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi celebrated Diwali with security forces in Chhattisgarh's Bastar. Modi said this was the first festival of lights when every district was free from Maoist insurgency. He credited the change in India's counter-insurgency strategy to the political will demonstrated after his government assumed office in 2014.

Article Title: 'Must maintain political neutrality': EC says model code curbs apply to retired govt officials
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: The Election Commission on Tuesday extended the Model Code of Conduct (MCC) restrictions to retired state government officials engaged by state governments in states where assembly elections are scheduled next year.In a letter addressed to the chief secretaries and chief electoral officers of Goa, Manipur, Punjab, Uttar Pradesh and Uttarakhand, the commission said such individuals must maintain political neutrality and refrain from participating in election campaigns."The Commission has in the past, in respect of the conduct of government employees, issued instructions stating that they are not expected to take part in any election campaign or canvassing and should take scrupulous care not to lend their names, official position or authority to assist one individual/political party/group as against another," the letter read."Individuals including retired government officials/officers/employees are attached or engaged or employed or re-employed in various capacities by State/UT governments, for whom there are no specific guidelines or rules relating to their political neutrality and conduct during MCC period," it added.Assembly elections are due in all five states in 2027, with polls expected to be held in February-March. The terms of the Manipur, Goa, Punjab and Uttarakhand assemblies end in March, while the Uttar Pradesh assembly's term expires in May.
Article Summary: The Election Commission extended the Model Code of Conduct (MCC) restrictions to retired state government officials. The commission said such individuals must maintain political neutrality and refrain from participating in election campaigns. Assembly elections are due in all five states in 2027, with polls expected to be held in February-March.

He said the decline had directly affected the local economy and promised to reverse the trend.“We will both improve and transform it. By introducing transparent administration at Ayodhya’s temple, we will also restore trust. By providing world-class infrastructure, we will make Ayodhya the ‘global capital of Sanatan pilgrimage’,” he said.The SP chief also promised measures to prevent the alleged mistreatment of poor people in the temple town, referring to an incident involving a woman and children collecting oil.“We will create an Ayodhya where no arrogant person can beat a poor woman or a boy or girl collecting oil and humiliate or oppress them,” he said.The SP chief further said that if voted to power, his government would provide oil and ghee through the public distribution system. “Once in government, we will also provide ‘oil and ghee’ in rations to meet the body’s nutritional needs,” he added.He further invoked the association between Lord Ram and Nishadraj, a central figure in the Ramayana tradition, and accused the BJP of attempting to undermine the relationship.“We will promote traditional boating in Ayodhya, so that traditional boatmen benefit from it and the deep bond between Lord Ram and Nishadraj can be restored,” he said.“The BJP wants to break this bond because BJP supremacists never want anyone to remember any scene of Lord Ram and the PDA community embracing one another,” Yadav added.PDA, or Pichhda, Dalit and Alpsankhyak (backward classes, Dalits and minorities), is the social coalition that the SP chief has been seeking to consolidate politically.Akhilesh also targeted alleged irregularities in land transactions and the circle rates in Ayodhya, promising scrutiny of land records and action against those responsible. “We will free Ayodhya from outside contractors and scrutinise land records. Outsiders are the ones who have looted Ayodhya,” he said.“No BJP leader or corrupt official involved in the massive circle-rate scam will escape. Their coffers, filled with the proceeds of Ayodhya’s plunder, will be emptied,” he added.The SP chief also called for legal action against people who insult religious deities and prominent figures, saying those who encourage such remarks should also be held accountable. “We will also create a system to ensure that no foul-mouthed person can insult the deities or great figures of any religion, let alone those of Lord Ram or Lord Krishna, or go about freely after doing so,” he said.Yadav further said that those encouraging people who make abusive remarks should also face consequences.“Those who encourage such wicked people who utter abusive words are also complicit in their sin, and they too will be punished appropriately for their involvement in a conspiracy to disrupt social harmony,” he said.Akhilesh's post came amid a political exchange over his proposed December 12 visit to Ayodhya, where he is scheduled to visit the Ram Temple and Hanumangarhi along with his wife, Dimple Yadav. The visit, announced by former SP MLA Pawan Pandey, would be Akhilesh's first to the Ram Temple since its inauguration in January 2024.Uttar Pradesh chief minister Yogi Adityanath on Saturday took an apparent swipe at the SP chief, saying those who had ordered firing on Ram devotees and subjected saints to lathicharge should apologise before visiting the temple.“Those who had neglected and insulted (Ayodhya), who had opened fire on Ram devotees and subjected saints to lathicharge, should certainly come to Ayodhya, but only after apologising. Let them apologise once to Ram devotees and once to the saints. Let them repent for their actions,” Adityanath said at the 10th edition of Deepotsav in Ayodhya, according to PTI.Although he did not name any person or the party, the remarks came hours after the announcement of the proposed temple visit.Read more: 'First apologise to devotees, saints' - UP CM Yogi ahead of Akhilesh Yadav's Ram Temple visit Recalling the Ram Janmabhoomi movement, Adityanath criticised previous governments over the firing on kar sevaks and the alleged neglect of Ayodhya.“There was a time when even uttering the name of Shri Ram in Ayodhya invited lathis and bullets. Banning the very name of Ram in this city was a sin. Ayodhya was neglected and almost consigned to oblivion. Today, that very Ayodhya has come alive again, reminding us of the Treta Yuga,” he said.
Article Summary: Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav vows to transform Ayodhya into the ‘global capital of Sanatan pilgrimage’ He pledges transparent temple administration, world-class infrastructure and measures to revive the local economy. Yadav also accused the BJP of weakening the bond between Lord Ram and the Nishad community. He warned that those involved in alleged land and circle-rate scams would face action.

Article Title: Fearing winter polls, Ladakh political parties, social bodies plan protests

Fearing winter polls, Ladakh political parties, social bodies plan protests

SRINAGAR: Political parties and civil society groups in Ladakh, apprehensive that the administration might hold Hill Council elections in Dec, on Monday said a winter election schedule would disenfranchise a significant section of the population as nearly 25% of Ladakhis migrate to other parts of the country during the harsh winter season.In Kargil, political parties and religious and social organisations called for a complete shutdown on Tuesday and a candlelight march in the evening, demanding deferment of the elections. In Leh, the Leh Apex Body (LAB) threatened to launch an agitation within the next few days. The administration, however, has not announced any dates for hill council polls as yet. Senior Ladakh administration officials were not available for comment.“For the past month we have been witnessing a series of notifications and orders and a flawed delimitation exercise. No one has been consulted or taken into confidence. The UT administration is once again imposing decisions on people,” Kargil Democratic Alliance (KDA) co-chairman Sajjad Kargili said at a news conference in Kargil. Flanked by Ladakh MP Mohmad Haneefa and other political and religious leaders, Kargili said 20% to 25% of Ladakh’s population, particularly elderly people, students and members of the business community, migrates outside the region during winter.Despite this, he said, the administration appears adamant about holding Hill Council elections in Dec. “This is an inappropriate and unwise decision.” Kargili said the people of Kargil have decided to observe a complete shutdown Tuesday.Haneefa said the proposed elections should not come at the cost of people’s democratic rights, pointing to harsh weather, difficult terrain, road closures and disrupted connectivity. Haneefa said he had urged the L-G to reconsider and defer the election schedule, allowing sufficient time for a comprehensive revision of electoral rolls and consultations with all stakeholders.In Leh, Leh Apex Body co-chairman Chering Dorjay Lakrook also urged the administration to postpone the elections until April or May next year, saying constituencies should first be properly delineated to ensure wider public participation.Addressing a news conference alongside members of All Goba Association and Ladakh Buddhist Association members, Lakrook said holding elections after winter would allow more people to participate. Lakrook also announced that the Leh Apex Body would launch an agitation within two to three days, saying the movement would demonstrate its public support. “We were supposed to be invited to the talks with the ministry of home affairs in Delhi on Oct 22, but we were not. The administration is taking us for granted. It is time for Ladakhis to wake up and stand up for their rights,” he said.
Article Summary: Fearing winter polls, Ladakh political parties, social bodies plan protests. Nearly 25% of Ladakhis migrate to other parts of the country during the harsh winter season. In Leh, the Leh Apex Body (LAB) threatened to launch an agitation within the next few days.

Article Title: 'Semantically ignorant': Congress defends Kharge's 'Diwali a khushiyon ki Eid' remark

NEW DELHI: The Congress and the BJP traded barbs over AICC president Mallikarjun Kharge 's description of Diwali as "khushiyon ka Eid", with the opposition party accusing the ruling party of deliberately misinterpreting his festive greeting.The row began after Kharge used the phrase while wishing people on Diwali over the weekend. The BJP objected to the comparison, arguing that Diwali should be referred to by its own name and accusing the Congress of being anti-Sanatani.BJP national media co-in-charge and spokesperson Pradeep Bhandari alleged that the Congress had brought vote-bank politics into Diwali celebrations by describing the festival as an "Eid of Happiness".Responding to the criticism, Congress media and publicity department head Pawan Khera said the BJP leaders had misunderstood the meaning of the word Eid."Those making a big deal out of Kharge ji’s statement are semantically ignorant," Khera said as per news agency PTI."The word 'Eid' literally means 'festival'. Now go and listen to his statement again. It is perfectly normal -- unlike the Sanghi negativity that makes some people incapable of sparing even a festival," Khera said on X.He also launched a sharp attack on those criticising Kharge, urging them to understand the meaning of the phrase rather than turn it into a controversy."In the spirit of Diwali and for the love of God, please light a bulb or two in your brain as well, and spare the rest of us the public display of your stupidity. Jaahil kahin ke (they are illiterates)," Khera added.BJP national spokesperson Gaurav Bhatia questioned why Kharge had compared Diwali, which he described as the biggest festival of Hindus, with Eid."Mr Kharge, what exactly is the problem with calling Diwali, the biggest festival of Hindus, by its own name?"Bhatia said Eid and Diwali each had their own religious significance and distinct traditions. He also challenged Kharge and Rahul Gandhi to explain whether they would describe Eid as the "Diwali of joy"."Has changing the identity of Hindu festivals become a matter of political etiquette in Congress's so-called secularism? Rahul Gandhi and Mr Kharge, answer this: will you ever have the courage to call Eid the "Diwali of joy," he asked."Respect Hindus' faith; don't change the identity of their festivals. Diwali was, Diwali is, and Diwali will remain Diwali," Bhatia said.Another BJP spokesperson, Tuhin Sinha , also criticised the Congress, saying Muslims celebrate Eid twice a year while the party wanted to describe every Hindu festival as "Khushiyon ki Eid".
Article Summary: AICC president Mallikarjun Kharge used the phrase while wishing people on Diwali over the weekend. The BJP objected to the comparison and accused the Congress of being anti-Sanatani. Congress leader Pawan Khera said the BJP leaders had misunderstood the meaning of the word Eid.

Article Title: US citizen shot by ICE officer near school bus stop sues Trump administration for $25m
Article Text:
Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agents work during a traffic stop (Representative image: AP).

Lawsuit alleges FBI interfered with medical treatment

Jimenez seeks more than $25 million in damages

A US citizen who was shot by an Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officer in the country’s southern California has filed a $25 million lawsuit against the federal government, accusing authorities of using excessive force, wrongfully arresting him and pursuing a case based on fabricated allegations.Carlos Jimenez was reportedly driving to work at a food pantry on October 30, 2025, when he encountered ICE officers conducting an operation in his neighbourhood. According to the complaint filed in federal court on Friday, Jimenez approached the officers around 7 am to warn them that children would soon be arriving at a nearby bus stop.According to the Guardian, the lawsuit alleges that an ICE officer, later identified as Eusebio Ortiz, pointed a gun at Jimenez's face, abused him verbally and threatened to shoot if he did not leave. The complaint cites audio recorded over the officer's radio.Jimenez then claimed to comply and attempted a three-point turn because officers' vehicles were blocking his way. However, Ortiz allegedly fired several shots into the car without warning, hitting Jimenez in the back and right shoulder.The complaint says no officer was in the vehicle's path when the shots were fired and alleges there was no reasonable suspicion or probable cause to stop, threaten or shoot Jimenez.The department of homeland security (DHS) had said at the time that Jimenez attempted to run over officers by reversing towards them without stopping. It described the officer's gunfire as “defensive” shots.Later, the justice department charged Jimenez with assaulting a federal officer using a deadly or dangerous weapon. The federal complaint alleged that he had “rapidly accelerated in reverse” towards an officer.According to the Guardian, the justice department's Los Angeles office has prosecuted 113 people for alleged offences against immigration officers since last spring. A Guardian review found that, as of mid-September, charges against 33 of them had been dismissed and nine others had been acquitted by juries.Jimenez's lawsuit describes the criminal allegations as “fabricated”. It also points out that, despite DHS's claim that the shooting was defensive, the criminal complaint did not include a statement from Ortiz saying he had felt threatened.The complaint further alleges that FBI agents followed Jimenez to the hospital and interfered with his medical care, including by pulling a nurse away and preventing him from speaking to medical staff.According to the lawsuit, agents removed him from his hospital bed, placed him in a waist restraint and took him back to the shooting site for questioning while a bullet was still lodged in his body.As per the complaint, Jimenez was bleeding and vomiting in the agents' van when officers told him not to “ruin their vehicle”.The lawsuit also accuses the FBI of falsely claiming that two neighbours witnessed the incident and told an agent that Jimenez had enough room to drive forward rather than reverse.However, Jimenez's lawyers allege that both witnesses denied making those statements when interviewed by the defence. They also said they had not known about the shooting until they saw reports about it in the media, according to the complaint.During the criminal proceedings, defence lawyers sought access to officers' text messages. A judge ordered the government to produce records of agents' communications in May, The Guardian reported.Prosecutors subsequently agreed to resolve the case through a diversion agreement, under which the charges could be dropped at the end of October if Jimenez met certain conditions. The lawsuit alleges that prosecutors sought to avoid the disclosure of communications and the questioning of an FBI agent accused of fabricating witness statements.The criminal charges were formally dismissed last week.The lawsuit seeks more than $25 million in damages, including compensation for lost wages and medical expenses. It alleges excessive force, assault, false arrest and other violations, and says Jimenez still has bullet fragments lodged near his lung.Justice department spokesperson Ciaran McEvoy did not comment on the lawsuit but said Jimenez “could have exercised his right to take the case to trial, but he instead requested that our office agree to resolve the case through a diversion agreement”.The case bears similarities to that of Francisco Longoria, another southern California resident who was shot by an ICE officer during a traffic stop last year and later faced criminal charges that were dropped.
Article Summary: Carlos Jimenez was reportedly driving to work at a food pantry on October 30, 2025, when he encountered ICE officers conducting an operation in his neighbourhood. Jimenez approached the officers around 7 am to warn them that children would soon be arriving at a nearby bus stop. ICE officer Eusebio Ortiz allegedly fired several shots into the car without warning, hitting Jimenez in the back and right shoulder.

No casualties were reported.In Dhaka, at least two crude bombs exploded in front of Tokyo Square in the Mohammadpur area around 9:15pm on Monday. Police said they were yet to identify those responsible.Separately, a Basumati Paribahan bus was set on fire in front of the Mirpur-11 Post Office around 9.30pm.No one was injured.In Bogura district, a van carrying jute sacks was set on fire on the Dhaka-Bogura highway in Sherpur upazila on Monday evening. The vehicle was gutted, temporarily disrupting traffic. Firefighters brought the blaze under control.More buses torched in Dhaka, Savar and GazipurThe incidents came amid a wider spate of arson attacks and crude bomb explosions across Bangladesh. According to The Daily Star, six buses were set on fire in Savar, Dhaka and Gazipur on Monday.In Savar, two buses parked along the Dhaka-Aricha highway were torched in the Genda and Baliarpur areas around 1am and 4am, respectively. One was used to transport garment workers, while the other belonged to Itihash Paribahan. The fires damaged the buses' seats and interiors.In Dhaka, a Lovely Paribahan bus was set on fire beneath the Farmgate metro station in the evening. Another bus, belonging to Basumati Paribahan, was torched under the metro rail line in Mirpur-11 around 9:15pm.In Gazipur's Kaliakair upazila, two parked buses were set on fire in the Chandra area along the Dhaka-Tangail highway, The Daily Star reported.Crude bomb explosions were also reported from several parts of Dhaka, including Banasree, Mohakhali, Dhaka University campus and outside the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate Court.Amid the attacks, the Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) set up 160 additional checkpoints at key locations across the capital on Monday and deployed more personnel to prevent further incidents.DMP Deputy Commissioner (Media) Akhter Hossain told The Daily Star that police had arrested at least 19 people in the preceding 24 hours in connection with recent blasts and attacks. He said many of those arrested were linked to the Awami League, whose activities are currently banned, reported The Daily Star.Police in Savar also suspected the involvement of the banned Awami League in the two bus arson incidents there. Investigations were under way to identify those responsible.The attacks come amid heightened political tensions in Bangladesh following the July 2024 uprising that led to the ouster of former prime minister Sheikh Hasina. The Awami League's activities were subsequently banned, and authorities have alleged links of some of its leaders and activists to recent incidents of crude bomb explosions and vehicle arson.
Article Summary: A 60-year-old bus driver was burnt to death after unidentified miscreants set fire to a parked bus in Bangladesh's Faridpur early Monday. A petrol bomb was hurled at a double-decker bus carrying around 35 students of Islamic University in Jhenaidah on Monday night. Six buses were set on fire in Savar, Dhaka and Gazipur on Monday. More than 50 crude bomb explosions were also reported from several parts of Dhaka.
