Article Title: Netanyahu's daily calls to Trump over Iran war spark pushback within White House: Report
Article Text:
Netanyahu is pressing Trump to restart Iran war as Arab leaders step up diplomatic efforts, report says.

Trump says Iran war is 'effectively over'

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has been calling US President Donald Trump every day to urge him to resume military action against Iran, even as Arab and Muslim leaders along with officials in White House step up efforts to prevent a fresh escalation and push Washington towards negotiations."Netanyahu calls him every day [to urge him to resume the war]. Those who don't want a war within the White House and outside have been trying to combat that," a person briefed on the discussions told the Financial Times.The person said regional leaders were urging Trump not to escalate the conflict and to prioritise negotiations. At least four Arab and Muslim leaders have spoken to the US president in recent days, seeking to persuade him to give diplomacy more time amid concerns that Washington could launch fresh strikes after last week's midterm elections.The leaders include Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, UAE President Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan, Qatar's Emir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani and Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan.Their efforts come as Trump has signalled that renewed US military action against Iran is unlikely for now, saying there is "positive momentum" towards ending the conflict.Trump made the remarks after meeting Qatari Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani at the White House on Monday.Vice-President JD Vance also attended the meeting. Qatar has been spearheading regional efforts to broker an interim agreement between Washington and Tehran.A diplomat briefed on the discussions described the meeting as "positive", saying there was agreement that diplomacy was the preferred way forward to reach a deal.Trump said Iran was militarily "effectively over" and indicated that a fresh US attack was not necessary at this stage. He nevertheless said American forces remained prepared to act if circumstances changed.In a post on Truth Social, Trump said there was "positive momentum toward an end to this Conflict", adding that the US would continue to protect its interests.He also said Qatar, Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Bahrain, Kuwait and other countries preferred the status quo, including the continuation of the US naval blockade of Iran.Trump's remarks come amid uncertainty over whether he would order fresh strikes after the midterm elections. The war and its impact on fuel prices were among the key issues for US voters, with Republicans suffering major losses in the polls.Although, Arab and Muslim leaders are concerned that renewed military action could plunge the region into a deeper crisis and trigger a strong Iranian response against neighbouring countries.Anwar Gargash, diplomatic adviser to the UAE president, said the priority should remain diplomatic efforts. "The priority must remain the pursuit of political diplomatic solutions capable of producing a more sustainable regional balance," he said.Gargash added that it was perhaps too early to assess the impact of the US midterm election results on Washington's approach towards Iran, but expressed hope that they would reinforce efforts to pursue diplomatic solutions and ensure stability in the Gulf.Iran, meanwhile, has warned that it is prepared to respond to any fresh attacks. It has also threatened to target undersea cables in the Strait of Hormuz and data centres in the region, raising concerns that any renewed confrontation could spread beyond the immediate conflict zone.The diplomatic push comes as mediators have struggled for weeks to break a deadlock between Washington and Tehran over an interim agreement.Both sides have been working with mediators on a proposal based on a version of a seven-day plan presented by Iran in September. Trump had rejected the proposal.
Article Summary: Netanyahu calls Trump every day to urge him to resume military action against Iran. Arab and Muslim leaders step up efforts to prevent a fresh escalation and push Washington towards negotiations. Trump has signalled that renewed US military action is unlikely for now, saying there is "positive momentum" towards ending the conflict.

Article Title: 1 year of Delhi blast: Al-Falah university, where module operated, fills all MBBS seats
Article Text:
Al-Falah University has filled its 200 MBBS seats, driven by a comprehensive governance reform





GURGAON: A year after the blast near Red Fort metro station claimed 15 lives and revealed a terrorist module being run by a group of doctors at Faridabad ’s Al-Falah University, its medical college has seen a reversal in fortunes.Now being run by a govt administrator, with the founder in prison, the college has filled all its 200 MBBS seats in the latest admission cycle, emerging from uncertainty about its future after intense scrutiny of its staff as well as students by investigating agencies.Academic activities have returned to normal at Al-Falah, with its affairs now directly under state govt’s watch following its takeover in March 2026. MBBS seats in the state are allotted through centralised counselling by Pt Bhagwat Dayal Sharma University of Health Sciences in Rohtak.IAS officer Amit Kumar Aggrawal was appointed administrator on March 21 this year. A team from JC Bose University of Science and Technology in Faridabad also took key posts.Ajay Ranga, registrar at JC Bose University, was given additional charge as Al-Falah’s vice-chancellor.Rajeev Kumar Singh, controller of examinations at JC Bose, was assigned the same role at Al-Falah, while Ravi Kumar Sharma was appointed chief finance and accounts officer and Meha Sharma was appointed registrar.Al-Falah founder-chairperson Jawad Ahmed Siddiqui was arrested in two separate cases of money laundering.An official credited the university’s turnaround to several measures taken after an inquiry found multiple statutory violations and irregularities in the functioning of the university.“The university now has around 80% of its faculty positions through advertisements in newspapers. Faculty members were earlier paid different salaries. The university now has introduced a uniform and improved salary structure, which has helped attract good professors,” said an official who is part of the govt-appointed administrative setup.“Before the incident, the university had faculty members who were associated with private clinics but were also registered as professors here but not actually teaching. They were paid for their association with Al-Falah. All such bogus faculty members have been removed. There is strict biometric attendance system now in place,” the official added. In the previous admission cycle, the university had filled 196 of its 200 seats.Al-Falah became the focus of an investigation by National Investigation Agency (NIA) after Dr Umer Un Nabi, who allegedly drove the i20 that blew up near Red Fort last Nov, was found to have worked there as an assistant professor.The agency’s chargesheet also alleged that Umer, his colleague Dr Muzammil Shakeel Ganaie and Dr Adeel Ahmed Rather tested explosives and firearms in villages in the vicinity, while Dr Shaheen Shahid helped finance weapons.According to NIA, the explosives were tested near a campus tubewell before trials shifted to fields and the Aravalis.Although the university denied any involvement of the institution as a whole, the investigation led to concerns among students that the college would shut down.The new administration also ordered fresh police checks of all students, employees and stakeholders, including those with incomplete records.“Everyone was scrutinised, every employee, every student and every stakeholder. We have re-verified everyone associated with the university. For those whose police verification reports were not available in our records, we have submitted their details again,” an official said.The official said no foreign student is currently enrolled at Al-Falah. A few from Dubai and Nepal had studied there earlier.“Yes, Al-Falah was at the centre of a terror investigation after the blast last year. But whatever inquiry is being conducted is being handled by respective agencies. The administration has no role in the probe,” the official said.
Article Summary: Al-Falah University has filled all its 200 MBBS seats in the latest admission cycle. The college has emerged from uncertainty about its future after intense scrutiny of its staff as well as students by investigating agencies. The university is now directly under state govt’s watch following its takeover in March 2026.

Article Title: 'Injured his own throat with scissors': New twist in Kolkata techie Sarthak Sarkar's murder case; girlfriend gives contradictory accounts
Article Text:
Sarthak’s live-in partner, Sanchalika Basu (22), and her mother, Moumita Basu, have been arrested.

Contradictory accounts complicate investigation

Argument over alleged relationships before murder

Neighbours heard screams, found man lying in blood

Poll Vote & Share your view What is the most important factor in preventing violent incidents during domestic disputes? More awareness campaigns Stronger laws and punishments Access to counselling services Community support networks 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion





KOLKATA: The investigation into the murder of 25-year-old software engineer Sarthak Sarkar in Kolkata remains inconclusive, with police yet to establish what was used to inflict the fatal injury to his throat and who delivered the blow.Investigators are examining whether a thin, pointed object, possibly a chopstick, was used in the attack. They are also trying to reconstruct the sequence of events inside the rented flat in Fartabad, Garia, where Sarkar was found critically injured late on Saturday night.Sarkar's live-in partner, Sanchalika Basu (22), and her mother, Moumita Basu, have been arrested in connection with the murder. However, police have not been able to establish a clear account of what happened, despite questioning the two women in custody.According to police, the mother and daughter have given contradictory statements during interrogation.Sanchalika allegedly told investigators at one point that Sarkar had injured his own throat with a pair of scissors. On another occasion, she reportedly said she could not remember what had happened during the heated argument.Investigators are trying to verify these claims and determine whether scissors or another sharp object was used in the attack.Police also suspect that Sarkar was assaulted during an argument with Sanchalika. They are examining the exact circumstances in which Moumita entered the room and whether she had any role in the attack.The couple had reportedly been quarrelling for some time over allegations of extramarital relationships.On Saturday night, an argument allegedly broke out between them while they were drinking. Both reportedly accused each other of being involved with multiple partners.Investigators suspect that the confrontation turned violent, leaving Sarkar with a fatal injury. However, the precise sequence of events and the role played by each of the two arrested women remain unclear.Sarkar, a resident of Barasat, had been living in the rented flat at Fartabad with Sanchalika. Her mother, Moumita, also stayed with them.Residents said they were alerted to the incident around 1.30 am when a woman ran out of the flat, crying and seeking help.“We were still awake when we heard a woman crying and asking for help. We immediately rushed to the flat and found a young man lying in a pool of blood on the bed. The woman who had sought our help had several scratch marks on her neck. We immediately informed the police,” said Sayan Pal, a Garia resident.He added that some occupants of the same building had heard a heated argument and loud noises coming from the flat shortly before the incident.Another local resident, Arkojeet Basu, said the couple had been living in the area for some time but rarely interacted with neighbours.“They did not mix much with people in the neighbourhood. We were shocked to learn about the incident in the morning,” he said.Sarkar was rushed to hospital, where doctors declared him dead. Police are continuing to question the arrested women and examine the evidence to establish how the attack took place.
Article Summary: Sarkar's live-in partner, Sanchalika Basu (22), and her mother, Moumita Basu, have been arrested. Police have not been able to establish a clear account of what happened, despite questioning the two women in custody.

Article Title: Woman killed with brick after argument with Facebook friend in Ghaziabad’s Loni
Article Text:
The deceased has been identified as Pinky, a native of Bulandshahr





GHAZIABAD: A woman was allegedly killed by a man she had befriended on Facebook around four to five months ago following an argument during their meeting in Ghaziabad’s Loni Border area on Monday.The deceased has been identified as Pinky, a native of Bulandshahr, while the accused, identified as Pintu, also hails from the same district.According to police, the incident came to light on Monday when the Indrapuri police outpost, under the Loni Border police station, received information about the murder of a woman. A police team, accompanied by senior officers, immediately reached the spot and inspected the crime scene.During preliminary inquiries, police discovered that Pinky and Pintu had come into contact through Facebook approximately four to five months ago. They subsequently began communicating over phone calls and developed a friendship.On Monday, Pintu reportedly visited Pinky to meet her. However, an argument broke out between them over an issue that is yet to be established.Police said the altercation escalated when Pintu allegedly picked up a brick lying nearby and struck Pinky on the head, causing fatal injuries.ACP Ankur Vihar Amardeep Maurya said the woman's body was taken into custody and sent for post-mortem examination after completing the necessary legal formalities."The two had become friends through Facebook around four to five months ago. The accused visited the woman on Monday, and an argument broke out between them. He allegedly attacked her on the head with a brick, resulting in her death," Maurya said.Police are questioning the accused to ascertain the circumstances surrounding the incident and the motive behind the alleged attack.Further legal proceedings are underway, while investigators are examining the sequence of events that led to the woman's death.
Article Summary: The deceased has been identified as Pinky, a native of Bulandshahr. The accused, identified as Pintu, also hails from the same district. The two had become friends through Facebook around four to five months ago.

Article Title: 1 killed as UP village head opens fire over gambling dispute; surrenders fearing encounter
Article Text:
Bakrabad village head Sanjay Bind, 40





VARANASI: One person was killed while another suffered a bullet injury after Bakrabad village head Sanjay Bind, 40, allegedly opened fire on them during a dispute over gambling in Mohav village under Kotwali police station limits in Ghazipur district late Monday night.Police teams began raiding possible hideouts of Bind, but he managed to reach Kotwali police station on Tuesday afternoon and surrendered before the police.Ghazipur ASP (City) Rakesh Kumar Mishra said around 10 people were gambling near a pond at Pasipurwa in Mohav village on Monday night. Around 10.30 pm, Bind and his associates joined them. Witnesses told police that after an argument broke out, Bind pulled out a pistol and opened indiscriminate fire.The bullets hit Ajay Pasi, 28, of Mohav, and Surendra Ram, 35, of Islamabad village, while Bind managed to escape. Both injured men were rushed to Ghazipur Medical College. However, doctors found their condition critical and referred them to the trauma centre at BHU in Varanasi. Ajay died during treatment, while Surendra, a mason, remained under treatment.On receiving information, Ghazipur SP Vinay Kumar Singh, Mishra and other officials reached the spot and also met the injured men at the hospital.Later, several teams were deployed to arrest Bind.However, fearing a police encounter, Bind reached Kotwali police station carrying a placard stating that he was surrendering and turned himself in on Tuesday afternoon. He told the police that he had won Rs 1.5 lakh while gambling and that others tried to snatch the money, leading to the firing.Police said Bind has several previous cases registered against him, including one for attacking a police team during Holi celebrations. He has two other criminal cases against him. Following the Holi incident, he was arrested and sent to jail. He was recently granted bail by the High Court and released from jail.
Article Summary: Bakarabad village head Sanjay Bind, 40, allegedly opened fire on them during a dispute over gambling. Ajay Pasi, 28, died during treatment, while Surendra Ram, 35, remained under treatment. Bind has several previous cases registered against him, including one for attacking a police team during Holi celebrations. He has two other criminal cases against him.

Article Title: Andhra Pradesh deputy chief minister Pawan Kalyan and wife Anna Konidela announce separation
Article Text:
K Pawan Kalyan and his wife, Anna Konidela, announced their separation on Monday.





VIJAYAWADA: Andhra Pradesh deputy chief minister K Pawan Kalyan and his wife, Anna Konidela, announced their separation on Monday, after 13 years of marriage, in a joint statement. Pawan Kalyan and Anna confirmed their decision in a joint statement issued through the Jana Sena’s official WhatsApp media group.“After sharing a significant part of our lives, we have decided to part ways with mutual understanding and respect. Though our marriage has come to an end, we remain good friends and devoted parents to our wonderful children. Their happiness and well-being will always remain our shared priority. During this personal transition, we seek your understanding, kindness, and respect for our privacy. We extend our heartfelt gratitude to everyone who has stood by us throughout this journey,” the joint statement issued by Pawan Kalyan and Anna Konidela read.Pawan married Anna Konidela (née Lezhneva), a Russian national, in Sept 2013, following his divorce from actress Renu Desai in 2012. The couple have a daughter and a son. Anna also acted alongside Pawan Kalyan in his film Teen Maar.Pawan married his first wife, Nandini, in Sept 1997. The couple separated in 1999 and divorced in 2008. He subsequently married actress Renu Desai in 2009, and they have a daughter and a son together.
Article Summary: Andhra Pradesh deputy chief minister K Pawan Kalyan and his wife, Anna Konidela, announced their separation on Monday. The couple confirmed their decision in a joint statement issued through the Jana Sena’s official WhatsApp media group. “We remain good friends and devoted parents to our wonderful children,” the statement read.

Article Title: 'I have decided not to contest': Jailed AAP MLA Laljit Singh Bhullar rules out 2027 polls via Facebook post
Article Text:
Laljit Singh Bhullar, an AAP MLA from Patti constituency, announced on social media he will not contest in 2027 elections (Photo credit: Facebook/@Laljit Singh Bhullar)





CHANDIGARH: In a significant political development ahead of the crucial 2027 Punjab assembly elections, jailed Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) MLA from Patti and former minister Laljit Singh Bhullar on Tuesday announced that he would not contest the next election, despite claims that people in his constituency wanted the party to field him again.In a social media post on Tuesday , Bhullar said he had heard the sentiments of people in Patti who wanted him to contest again, but had decided against entering the electoral fray.He expressed gratitude towards the people for their love, affection and continued support, saying he would remain indebted to them throughout his life.Sources informed that Bhullar's supporters had approached the AAP leadership urging them to give him party ticket to contest the 2027 assembly elections."I have heard the sentiments expressed by the brothers and sisters of the Patti constituency regarding the party fielding me once again in the upcoming elections. However, I have decided not to contest the election," he wrote."I bow my head in deep respect before your love, affection and sentiments. I shall remain indebted to the people of Patti constituency throughout my life," he added.Bhullar's announcement comes amid uncertainty over his political future following his arrest in connection with the suicide of Dr Gagandeep Singh Randhawa, district manager of the Punjab State Warehousing Corporation in Amritsar.Randhawa allegedly died by suicide on March 21, 2026, after levelling serious allegations against Bhullar. Amritsar police arrested Bhullar from Mandi Gobindgarh on March 23.The victim's family had earlier refused to cremate Randhawa's body until Bhullar was arrested.Bhullar's decision is also significant as his wife, Surinderpal Kaur, had become politically active in Patti following her husband's arrest and was reportedly staking a claim to the AAP ticket.The party had meanwhile appointed wrestler Jassa Patti as constituency in-charge in view of Bhullar's continued incarceration, leaving his wife go poloticlly silent.Notably, in the 2022 assembly elections, Bhullar had won the Patti seat with 57,323 votes, defeating his nearest rival, SAD candidate Adesh Partap Singh Kairon, who secured 46,324 votes.
Article Summary: Laljit Singh Bhullar, an AAP MLA from Patti constituency, announced on social media he will not contest in 2027 elections. He said he had heard the sentiments of people in Patti who wanted him to contest again, but had decided against entering the electoral fray. His decision comes amid uncertainty over his political future following his arrest in connection with the suicide of Dr Gagandeep Singh Randhawa.

Article Title: Mumbai local train stabbing: Accused claims real 'killer' fled, says he was a bystander
Article Text:
The family says Suvarna was traced through technical evidence, a doctor linked the injuries to the weapon, and the knife seller identified him.





MUMBAI: Roshan Suvarna, 30, arrested for allegedly stabbing 22-year-old Mayank Lohar to death inside a moving local train, has sought bail, claiming he was merely a bystander injured while trying to stop a fight between Lohar and an unidentified man.Suvarna's plea says he intervened in the quarrel, suffered injuries, and was falsely implicated after the alleged attacker fled. Lohar's family has opposed bail, saying they fear for their safety and for witnesses. The plea will be heard on Nov 20.Through advocate Prince Kumar Upadhyay, Lohar's father, Ramesh Lohar, filed an intervention plea describing the attack as a cruel, unprovoked murder."A young man of 22 was killed in a public train over a trivial quarrel. His parents have lost their son," the reply said, adding that releasing Suvarna would prejudice the prosecution and erode public confidence in commuter safety. The incident occurred late on June 23, 2026, on a Nalasopara-bound fast local from Andheri.Police said Lohar was returning from work when a dispute began near the door after rainwater splashed into the compartment.Passengers separated the men. After the alarm chain was pulled between Goregaon and Malad, the assailant allegedly stabbed Lohar in the chest and abdomen.He was taken to Shatabdi Hospital, where he was declared dead before admission.The family's reply says Lohar was unarmed and had not assaulted anyone. It alleges that, about eight minutes after passengers intervened, Suvarna walked to Lohar's new position, took a knife from his bag and stabbed him multiple times on vital parts, then threatened passengers before fleeing.The defence says Suvarna and Lohar were strangers, there was no motive or premeditation, no weapon was recovered from Suvarna, and CCTV did not show the stabbing. It also questioned the test identification parade.The family says Suvarna was traced through technical evidence, a doctor linked the injuries to the weapon, and the knife seller identified him. It says no medical proof supports his injury claim.
Article Summary: Roshan Suvarna, 30, arrested for allegedly stabbing 22-year-old Mayank Lohar to death inside a moving local train. He has sought bail, claiming he was merely a bystander injured while trying to stop a fight between LOHar and an unidentified man. The family has opposed bail, saying they fear for their safety. The plea will be heard on Nov 20.

Article Title: Diwali revellers kill cop, techie in separate Tamil Nadu incidents
Article Text:
On Diwali night in Tamil Nadu, two individuals were killed during disputes over firecrackers





COIMBATORE: Two people were killed in Tamil Nadu on Diwali night following arguments over bursting firecrackers, with a SI beaten to death in Theni district and an IT company employee stabbed in Trichy district.Police said special SI Senthil Kumar, 56, attached to Theni DSP’s office, was returning home in plain clothes after duty when he noticed a group of youths, allegedly under the influence of alcohol, bursting crackers on the road at Samatharmapuram.He warned the youths against obstructing traffic, but they allegedly paid no heed. When Senthil started recording their activities on his phone, they assaulted him. As the SSI collapsed on the road, the youths fled, police said. The cop later died in hospital.Cops arrested six persons on murder and other charges. CM C Joseph Vijay announced a solatium of Rs 40 lakh for the deceased cop’s family.The second murder was reported from Purathakudi village in Trichy. The victim, X Christopher, who worked as a technician with an IT company in Chennai, had come home to celebrate Diwali.On Sunday night, C Donald, 20, and J Edison, 20, residents of the same village, were passing through the street where Christopher and his friend Ranjith were bursting crackers.The duo picked up a fight with Christopher and his friend, claiming that splinters of crackers had fallen on them.As the argument escalated, Donald, an electrician, suddenly took out a tester screwdriver and stabbed Christopher on the left side of his chest and back.When Ranjith attempted to intervene and save his friend, Donald and Edison assaulted him before fleeing the scene.
Article Summary: Two people were killed in Tamil Nadu on Diwali night following arguments over bursting firecrackers. A special SI was beaten to death in Theni district and an IT company employee was stabbed in Trichy district. CM C Joseph Vijay announced a solatium of Rs 40 lakh for the deceased cop's family.

Article Title: 'Demonic mentality': Toddler raped inside abandoned building in Goa; minister blames 90% of such crimes on ‘outsiders’
Article Text:
Image Used For Representational Purpose Only

Pilots saw accused with child, thought he was family member





GOA: A three-to-four-year-old child was allegedly raped inside an abandoned building near Lohia Ground in Mapusa on Diwali night, with police yet to trace the accused.The girl, who belongs to a family of balloon sellers, was found injured and has been shifted to Goa Medical College and Hospital for treatment. Mapusa police detained a couple of suspects by Monday afternoon.Chief minister Pramod Sawant said that it will be ensured the accused is “kept permanently behind bars”.“People with such mentality should not exist in our society. Police will take strict action and ensure that he goes behind bars permanently,” he said.The girl was found by a group of motorcycle pilots stationed at a stand near the abandoned building. Tribal welfare minister Ramesh Tawadkar claimed “90 per cent” of such crimes in the tourist state are committed by “outsiders”. Such crimes should not happen in Goa or anywhere else in the country, he told PTI.Minister Ramesh Tawadkar said, “The person who has committed this crime has a demonic mentality. Goa is a tourist state. People from outside the state come here and 90% of people involved in such cases are those who have come to Goa from outside,” he added.However, he maintained people could not be stopped from coming to Goa to earn their livelihood.Around 8 pm on Diwali night, a group of motorcycle pilots had initially noticed a man holding the crying child’s hand and escorting her towards the area. However, assuming he was a family member, they did not suspect anything amiss. “We are used to balloon sellers roaming around here during the festive season with little children accompanying them. The child was crying, but walking away with him. So we thought he was known to her and the child was just fussing. We felt bad later, thinking we could have prevented it if we had realised his intentions. We were focused on getting customers when we saw him. But one pilot did call out to the man, asking him to take care of the child. Later, a pilot noticed the girl coming out crying from the abandoned building,” said Pundalik Neurekar, a motorcycle pilot and eyewitness.The girl emerged from the building around 1.5 hours later. The pilots initially assumed she was crying because she had been separated from her family. They kept her with them and tried to pacify her.A woman working at a nearby tailoring shop then noticed the child and gave her a cloth to wrap herself in. On noticing blood on her, the pilots realised she may have been sexually assaulted and alerted the police.A Mapusa police team combed the area around 4 am in search of the accused, but the operation yielded no results. A forensic team collected samples from the crime scene on Monday morning.Police have also obtained CCTV footage from shops in Mapusa market and surrounding areas in an effort to identify the accused. “The man was wearing a jacket. He did not appear to be a local from around here, and he had a backpack on him,” said another motorcycle pilot, Mangaldas Gawas.
Article Summary: A three-to-four-year-old child was allegedly raped inside an abandoned building near Lohia Ground in Mapusa on Diwali night. The girl, who belongs to a family of balloon sellers, was found injured and has been shifted to Goa Medical College and Hospital for treatment. Police detained a couple of suspects by Monday afternoon.

Article Title: Out on bail in 1st case, Mangaluru priest now faces 2nd POCSO case involving 13-year-old boy
Article Text:
65-year-old Father Cyprian Pinto, a Catholic priest, is now implicated in a second sexual assault case involving a minor

Earlier POCSO case against Father Cyprian Pinto





MANGALURU: A 65-year-old Catholic priest in Mangaluru has been booked in a second case over allegations of sexually assaulting a minor boy, weeks after he was arrested in a separate case involving another teenager.The latest complaint accuses Father Cyprian Pinto of sexually assaulting a 13-year-old boy in May this year, police said.The case was registered at Mangaluru Women Police Station following a complaint alleging that the incident took place on May 13, 2026.According to the complaint, the boy, a resident of Permannur village, regularly attended Sunday prayers at a church. The alleged assault took place when he was associated with the church, police said.Police have registered a case under Section 75(2) (sexual harassment) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) and Sections 8 and 12 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act.Further investigation has been entrusted to the Assistant Commissioner of Police (ACP), Central Sub-Division.Mangaluru City Police Commissioner Sudheer Kumar Reddy CH confirmed that the second complaint had been registered and said the ACP, Central Sub-Division, was conducting further investigation.The latest complaint comes weeks after another case was registered against the same priest at Mangaluru South Police Station on October 15 over allegations of sexually harassing a 14-year-old boy.In that case, Pinto was arrested and produced before a court on October 18. He was remanded to judicial custody until October 30 and was subsequently released on bail.The investigation into the earlier case is still underway.Police have not disclosed further details of the investigation in the latest case.(With PTI inputs)
Article Summary: Father Cyprian Pinto, a Catholic priest, is now implicated in a second sexual assault case involving a minor boy. The latest complaint accuses Pinto of sexually assaulting a 13-year-old boy in May this year. The case was registered at Mangaluru Women Police Station following a complaint alleging that the incident took place on May 13.

Article Title: Blood offering, flying stones: Himachal's Dhami village keeps 400-year-old ritual 'Patthar Ka Khel' alive
Article Text:
Dhami village in Himachal Pradesh observes a unique stone-pelting ritual called 'Patthar Ka Khel' after Diwali

Why do villagers pelt each other with stones?





SHIMLA: Stones fly, crowds gather and a few drops of blood become an offering to the goddess. Himachal Pradesh's Dhami village witnessed its annual 'Patthar Ka Khel', a nearly 400-year-old stone-pelting ritual celebrated on the day after Diwali.A large number of people gathered to witness the unusual tradition, in which two groups of villagers throw stones at each other until a participant sustains a minor injury.Following the ritual, a few drops of blood from the injured participant are offered to Goddess Bhadrakali as part of the centuries-old custom.The tradition is believed to have originated as an alternative to human sacrifice, which was practised centuries ago to appease the deity.The ritual was associated with seeking protection from diseases, natural calamities and other misfortunes.Celebrated every year after Diwali, the nearly four-century-old practice continues to draw large crowds to Dhami, where villagers gather to participate in and witness the traditional ceremony.(With ANI inputs)
Article Summary: Dhami village in Himachal Pradesh observes a stone-pelting ritual called 'Patthar Ka Khel' after Diwali. A few drops of blood from the injured participant are offered to Goddess Bhadrakali as part of the centuries-old custom.

Article Title: 2nd marriage, locked house, unanswered calls: Mystery shrouds deaths of Nagpur couple
Article Text:
The deceased were identified as Manish Ganvir (38) and his wife, Sonali (35).

Relative alerted police after family failed to reach couple

Neighbours heard argument before house fell silent

No suicide note recovered





NAGPUR: A couple, both schoolteachers, were found dead at their home in Nagpur's Besa area on Sunday, days after returning from Gadchiroli to celebrate Diwali.The deceased were identified as Manish Pralhad Ganveer, 38, and his wife Sonali Ganveer, 35.The couple, who married in August this year, worked as teachers at a school in Surjagad in Gadchiroli district.Their bodies were found hanging from a ceiling fan in the bedroom of their house in Revati Nagar, a Beltarodi police official said.Police said the couple had been alone at home after Manish's family left for Bihar a day earlier. When repeated attempts to contact them went unanswered, family members sent a relative to check on them on Sunday.The relative found the house locked from outside.He managed to reach the first floor and looked through a window, where he spotted the couple hanging from the ceiling fan, each with a separate scarf.According to police, neighbours heard the couple arguing loudly around 3.30 pm on Friday.Police said this was the second marriage for both Manish and Sonali. Both had experienced troubled marriages before deciding to start afresh together.No suicide note was found at the house, police said.Investigators are attempting to access the couple's mobile phones to establish the circumstances surrounding their deaths.The bodies were sent for post-mortem examinations. Senior officers from Beltarodi police station visited the house and began an investigation.Police have not yet established what led to the deaths.
Article Summary: Manish Ganvir, 38, and his wife Sonali Ganveer, 35, found dead at home. Neighbours heard argument before house fell silent. No suicide note was found at the house in Nagpur's Besa area.

Article Title: 'Bullet pierced through chest': Newlywed wrestler shot dead while bursting crackers outside home in Punjab
Article Text:
The deceased, Mani alias Pehalwan, who got married around six months back, was bursting firecrackers outside his house





KAPURTHALA: A 27-year-old wrestler was shot dead on Monday night while bursting crackers at his house in Kapurthala town.The deceased, Mani alias Pehalwan, who got married around six months back, was bursting firecrackers outside his house in the Mehtabgarh area when armed assailants fired at him around 7.30 pm.At least one bullet pierced through his chest and he collapsed.He was rushed to Civil Hospital, Kapurthala, but he had died before reaching there. Police have started an investigation.DSP Shital Singh said that the dispute was between two groups and a neighbour of the deceased youth was the target of the assailants.The DSP said that the deceased's father Bagga said that they did not have enmity with anybody.He said that the statement of the family was being recorded and the investigation was on.
Article Summary: The deceased, Mani alias Pehalwan, who got married around six months back, was bursting firecrackers outside his house in the Mehtabgarh area. At least one bullet pierced through his chest and he collapsed. He was rushed to Civil Hospital, Kapurthala, but he died before reaching there.

Article Title: Car hits electricity pole, tears through divider and catches fire; 6 friends burnt alive in UP
Article Text:
Six individuals lost their lives in a devastating car crash on the Panipat-Khatima national highway





HANSI: Six people from Haryana ’s Hansi district were burnt to death after their car crashed into an electricity pole, breached a road divider and overturned before catching fire on the Panipat-Khatima national highway in Uttar Pradesh’s Muzaffarnagar district early Monday.The deceased — Aman (21) and Ajay (21), both from Moth Rangran village, and Sahil, Ankit (21), brothers Ankit (21) and Rahul (23), all from Rakhigarhi village — were travelling to Haridwar to take a holy dip on Somvati Amavasya.The accident occurred around 5 am near Jaggaheri village, under the jurisdiction of Titawi police station, about 25 km from Muzaffarnagar district headquarters.According to preliminary information, the car was at high speed when the driver lost control of the vehicle. The car first rammed into an electricity pole, breaking it into two pieces, before crashing through nearly 10 metres of the road divider and overturning on the opposite carriageway.The vehicle caught fire soon after the collision, with flames engulfing it within minutes.Firefighters struggled for nearly an hour to bring the blaze under control. However, all six occupants had died by then. The bodies were severely charred, making identification difficult.Aman, Ajay and one of the Ankits were students, while the other Ankit worked as an AC and refrigerator repair technician. Rahul was reportedly a gas pipeline mechanic.Police said the vehicle belonged to a relative of Sahil, who had borrowed it two days before the accident.Police said the families of the deceased had been informed, and further legal proceedings were underway.
Article Summary: Six people from Haryana ’s Hansi district were burnt to death after their car crashed into an electricity pole, breached a road divider and overturned. The accident occurred on the Panipat-Khatima national highway in Uttar Pradesh’s Muzaffarnagar district early Monday.

Article Title: Assam man hacks woman inside car, dumps body in ditch near temple
Article Text:
Baishya’s body was recovered near a temple in Khanapara on Saturday.





GUWAHATI: Police arrested a driver on Monday for allegedly hacking a woman to death and dumping her body in a sack in Khanapara.The accused, Pradeep Taye (45) of Dhemaji district, and the deceased, Jeena Baishya (32) of Koinadhara, were allegedly in an extramarital relationship for 10 years. Police suspect frequent disputes between them may have led to the murder.Baishya’s body was recovered near a temple in Khanapara on Saturday. Her husband, Jeetu Baishya, lodged a complaint at Basistha Police Station earlier that day, following which a murder case was registered.“The woman’s body was recovered near Ganesh temple on Saturday. On the same day, before the recovery, her husband had lodged a complaint at Basistha police station. A case was registered under the relevant sections of the law pertaining to murder,” said Basistha OC Kapil Pathak.Pathak said the case initially appeared to be a no-clue murder, but circumstantial and other evidence led to Taye’s arrest in Koinadhara.“Following the arrest, we seized a vehicle, the machete used in the crime and other items that were connected to this incident,” he said.Police allege that Taye picked up Baishya from Basistha on the day of the incident and drove her around for several hours. He allegedly took her to an isolated spot near the temple around 8 pm, attacked her with a weapon inside the vehicle and dumped her body in a nearby ditch.Police said the investigation is continuing. Taye was produced before a local court on Monday and remanded in 2-day police custody.
Article Summary: Pradeep Taye (45) of Dhemaji district, and the deceased, Jeena Baishya (32) of Koinadhara, were allegedly in an extramarital relationship for 10 years. Police suspect frequent disputes between them may have led to the murder. The body was recovered near a temple in Khanapara on Saturday.

KANPUR: A 55-year-old LIC agent was killed after a Mahindra Thar allegedly driven by a woman pursuing her studies in Italy hit his scooter and dragged him and the vehicle for nearly 20 metres in Uttar Pradesh's Kanpur, police said.The woman, identified as Eeta Sachan, was arrested following the accident and later released by a court.The victim, Santosh Singh Chauhan, was returning home after stepping out to buy a saree for his wife. He was barely 500 metres from his house when the accident took place on Saturday evening in the Awas Vikas 3 area of Kalyanpur.Chauhan, a resident of Swaraj Nagar in Panki, was riding his scooter when the speeding SUV rammed into him. The impact dragged him and his vehicle for around 20 metres before the Thar crashed into a green area outside a house.The SUV first struck the house of Professor Kailash before crashing into the boundary wall of Anita Mahevan's house, residents said.Chauhan's son, Rahul, identified his father's body. He said his father had left home telling the family that he would be back shortly.Occupants allegedly leave spot in another carWitnesses said two young women and a man travelling in the Thar screamed after the collision but later left the spot in another car.The SUV, which had 'Kisan Union' written on its front and 'Krishna Group' on its rear, was seized by police. Two helmets were also recovered from the accident spot.Station house officer Keshav Tiwari said police had taken possession of the vehicle and were collecting CCTV footage from the area to establish the sequence of events.The investigation is under way.

KRISHNAGIRI: Three contract workers died after drowning while carrying out maintenance and cleaning work inside a nano-filtration feed tank at Tata Marigold Company in Vanniyapuram, in Krishnagiri district on Monday evening.The deceased have been identified as Kaveri, 28, J Akmal, 28, and Sarath Kumar, 25, all from Rayakottai.
